question: True or false: in a fire, structural steel has lost about half its strength by the time it reaches 600 °C?
answer: True. Steel melts near 1,500 °C but only has to soften to fail. By the European design code it keeps full strength to 400 °C, 47% at 600 °C and 23% at 700 °C; a standard test fire passes 840 °C in half an hour. Hence the fireproofing sprayed on steel beams.
move: Ask when a thing stops doing its job, not when it disappears.
trap: Steel stays strong until it melts, far above any room fire.

diagram.caption: Far below its melting point, hot steel has already lost half its strength.

reference: EN 1993-1-2:2005, Eurocode 3: Design of steel structures — Part 1-2: General rules — Structural fire design
